qa.question: If the Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards is itself blue, does this card’s inherited effect activate?
qa.answer: Yes, if a Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards is itself blue, the effect activates.

qa.question: Does this card’s [On Play] effect force me to reveal 3 cards from the top of my deck?
qa.answer: Yes. The effect reads, "Reveal the top 3 cards of your deck," so if possible, you must reveal 3 cards. If you have fewer than 3 cards left in your deck, reveal as many as you can.

qa.question: This card's [On Play] effect reveals cards from the top of my deck. If I reveal a card with [Free] in its traits, do I have to add it to my hand?
qa.answer: Yes. The effect reads, “Add 1 card...to your hand,” so if you reveal a card that meets the requirements, you must add it to your hand.

qa.question: If the Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards is itself green, does this card’s inherited effect activate?
qa.answer: Yes, if a Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards is itself green, the effect activates.

qa.question: Does this card’s [When Digivolving] effect activate when performing a non-DNA digivolve?
qa.answer: No, it only activates when DNA digivolving.

qa.question: If there’s both a level 4 or lower blue Digimon card and a level 4 or lower green Digimon card in this Digimon’s digivolution cards, does this card’s [When Digivolving] effect require me to play both of them?
qa.answer:
No. The effect reads, “you may,” so you can choose whether to play them. However, if you choose to play them, you must play as many cards as possible.
If there are both a level 4 or lower blue Digimon card and a level 4 or lower green Digimon card in the digivolution cards, you can't choose to only play one of them.

qa.question: My opponent attacks with a Digimon and deletes my only blue Digimon with its [When Attacking] effect. I have no other blue Digimon in play, but can I still block the attack with this Digimon?
qa.answer: No. The [When Attacking] effect activates before reaction timing, which is when <Blocker> triggers. By the time reaction timing occurs, this Digimon no longer has <Blocker>, so it cannot block.

qa.question: How does this card’s inherited effect work, exactly?
qa.answer: At the end of your turn, this effect allows you DNA digivolve a Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards, along with one of your other Digimon, into a Digimon in your hand that has [DNA Digivolve]. Note that this happens before it becomes your opponent’s turn.

qa.question: With this card's inherited effect, can I DNA digivolve into a Digimon card in my hand that doesn’t have [DNA Digivolve]?
qa.answer: No. You can’t ignore the digivolution requirements, so you can’t DNA digivolve into a Digimon card that doesn’t have [DNA Digivolve].

qa.question: Does this card's inherited effect allow me to DNA digivolve into a card other than the Digimon specified by [DNA Digivolution] in the hand?
qa.answer: No. You can’t ignore the digivolution requirements, so you can’t DNA digivolve using Digimon that aren’t specified in [DNA Digivolution].

qa.question: If the Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards is itself blue, does this card’s inherited effect activate?
qa.answer: Yes, if a Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards is itself blue, the effect activates.

qa.question: Can I play this Digimon with its [Security] effect even if it loses the battle against the attacking Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, regardless of the battle's outcome, you get to play this Digimon at the end of the battle.

qa.question: Does this card’s [On Play] effect activate when played with this card’s [Security] effect?

This card is flipped over during a security check, but the attacking Digimon still has security checks remaining. Does this Digimon’s effect activate first, or do I have to wait until my opponent finishes the rest of their security checks?
qa.answer:
This Digimon is played after the battle with the attacking Digimon, and before the next check is performed.
Likewise, this Digimon’s [On Play] effect activates before your opponent’s next check.

qa.question: Does this card’s [When Digivolving] effect activate when performing a non-DNA digivolve?
qa.answer: When performing a non-DNA digivolve, only the “Suspend 1 of your opponent’s Digimon” part of the effect activates. The part of the effect that reads, “that Digimon doesn't unsuspend during its owner’s next unsuspend phase” only activates when DNA digivolving.

qa.question: Does this card’s inherited effect also count the colors of its digivolution cards?
qa.answer: No, only the colors of the top card are counted. If the card is a mono-colored Digimon card, it will be counted as a single color, even if its digivolution cards are different colors.

qa.question: I use this card’s effect to suspend 1 of my opponent’s Digimon. Can I then use this effect to return a different suspended Digimon to its owner’s hand?
I use this card’s effect to give 1 of my Digimon +2000 DP. Can I then use this effect to give another Digimon <Piercing>?

comprehensive-0223.title: <Blocker>
comprehensive-0223.text:
16-5. <Blocker>
16-5-1. <Blocker> is a keyword effect that applies a rule that allows a Digimon with that effect to block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")
16-5-2. <Blocker> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-5-3. Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Blocker>, the number of blocks that can be performed during the block timing is only 1.

comprehensive-0225.title: <Piercing>
comprehensive-0225.text:
16-7. <Piercing>
16-7-1. <Piercing> is a keyword effect that reads "When this Digimon deletes your opponent's Digimon in battle while attacking, it checks security before the attack ends." (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")
16-7-2. <Piercing> is a trigger-type effect that triggers and activates when a Digimon with this effect battles an opponent's Digimon and the opponent's Digimon is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger- Type Effects")
16-7-3. The security check from using <Piercing> is mandatory.
16-7-4. <Piercing> is pending processing that is processed immediately before the transition to the end of attack timing. Therefore, it will trigger simultaneously with effects triggered by the battle, but it is processed before the end of the attack. (Example: If a Digimon with <Piercing> attacks and deletes a Digimon with an [On Deletion] effect in the battle, first the [On Deletion] effect is resolved, then <Piercing> is processed.)
16-7-5. Only 1 security check can be performed during a single attack, even if <Piercing> activates multiple times. However, if the number of cards that can be checked by the attacking Digimon is modified, that number of cards will be checked in a single security check.
16-7-6. If there are no Digimon to perform a security check at the point when <Piercing> is processed, a security check won't be possible.

comprehensive-0226.title: <Draw>
comprehensive-0226.text:
16-8. <Draw>
16-8-1. <Draw> is a keyword effect where a player draws the cards from their deck according to the number specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Draw 1>.
16-8-2. <Draw> effects execute processing.
16-8-3. A draw from <Draw> is mandatory.
